explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/388: are there only finitely many solutions of ∏_{1≤i≤k₁}(m₁+i) = ∏_{1≤j≤k₂}(m₂+j) with k₁, k₂ > 3 and m₁ + k₁ ≤ m₂? The Lean statement asserts finiteness of the set of (m₁, k₁, m₂, k₂) ∈ ℕ⁴ with exactly these conditions; taking m₁, m₂ ≥ 0 (as the docstring explains) rules out trivial sign-flipped solutions and matches the intended positive blocks. 'Yes' form per the question convention. Faithful.
